description: **Role Overview** We are looking for a Systems Software Engineer to work on the software that runs on our embedded devices - from board bring-up and low-level driver work through to complete, deployable applications. A significant part of the role is integration: bringing multiple peripherals and sensors into a single system and making them work together reliably. That means writing the interface layers, getting the data flowing correctly and on time, and then proving the whole thing holds up under real operating conditions. The role suits an engineer who is comfortable close to the hardware, who reads a datasheet before writing code, and who enjoys the point where software, electronics and sensors meet. **Key Responsibilities** - Develop and bring up complete embedded system applications, from initial board bring-up to deployed software. - Integrate multiple peripherals and sensors into a working system — writing interface and driver-level code, and validating behaviour against hardware. - Implement communication over standard interfaces and buses (I2C, SPI, UART, CAN, USB, Ethernet and similar), including protocol handling, framing and error recovery. - Build reliable data paths between subsystems, handling timing, buffering, synchronisation and throughput constraints. - Write multi-threaded and concurrent code, with careful attention to synchronisation, shared state and real-time behaviour. - Optimise software for speed, memory footprint and deterministic performance across target platforms. - Diagnose and fix bugs, race conditions and performance bottlenecks, including issues that only appear on real hardware. - Work with image and video data paths where required — capture, buffering and processing. - Collaborate with hardware, firmware, algorithms and systems teams to define, design and ship new features. - Maintain high coding standards, with clean, reviewable and testable code. - Travel to client sites as needed to support integration, commissioning and field debugging. **Qualifications** - Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Electronics, Electrical Engineering or a related technical field. - Proven professional experience in C and C++, particularly in embedded or systems-level software. - Strong background in embedded application and firmware development, with examples of prior work. - Practical experience integrating peripherals and sensors, and working directly from datasheets and interface specifications. - Solid understanding of multi-threading and concurrent programming, and the failure modes that come with them. - Comfortable working in Linux, including cross-compilation and building for embedded targets. - Strong debugging instincts and analytical skills, especially where the problem sits between software and hardware. - Clear communication, including the ability to explain technical detail to non-technical stakeholders. - Willingness and ability to travel for client engagements. **Preferred Skills** - Experience with image processing, video pipelines or camera interfaces. - Familiarity with device drivers, kernel-space development or RTOS environments. - Working knowledge of Python for test, automation and analysis tooling. - Version control with Git, and familiarity with modern build systems such as CMake. - Experience with unit, integration and automated testing frameworks. - A track record of designing and implementing systems that scale and stay maintainable. - Sound grounding in professional software engineering practice across the full development life cycle.

description: **About us** Deepvue.ai builds identity, risk, fraud, and compliance infrastructure on India's digital public infrastructure. We're expanding beyond verification into AI for risk and decisioning products for financial services. **The role** We move fast on new ideas. Someone takes a problem from nothing to a working prototype, we put it in front of customers, and then it needs to become a real product — extended, hardened, configurable, and built out across every case a customer actually has. You'd start on that second half, because it's how you learn the systems and the customers fastest. Six months in, once you have that, you'd be starting things yourself too — taking a problem from zero rather than only building it out. **What that looks like day to day** - Building out new product surfaces from prototype to production - Customer-specific configurations and variants — the same components assembled differently for different requirements - Extending the existing API platform, and the APIs behind our dashboards and customer-facing interfaces - Building and scaling AI/ML and GenAI pipelines from experimental workflows into production systems - Working across the stack, from backend services to product SDKs, to get AI features into user-facing applications - Owning critical product components end to end — you're accountable for them being robust in production, not just merged - Increasingly, your own problems to take from nothing The scope widens as we ship. Whatever gets validated next lands with you, so this isn't a fixed queue of work — it grows with the company, and so does what you own. You'll ship a lot. That's the point of the role. **Our stack** Python (Django, FastAPI) across most of the platform, with some services in Go. TypeScript on the front end. MySQL, Postgres, MongoDB, Docker, AWS. On the AI side, LLM APIs and agentic frameworks, with vector stores and retrieval where the problem calls for it. CI/CD and an observability stack — you'll instrument your own services. **What we actually need from you** - **Strong Python, with Django or FastAPI in production.** That's what we'll expect you to be fluent in on day one. Expect to pick up Go alongside it — some of what you'll build lives there - **Enough TypeScript to build the interface your API feeds.** Working forms, tables and flows against a component library. You're not designing, and we're not expecting polish - **AWS, hands-on.** You'll deploy your own work, instrument it, and be the one who notices when it breaks. Containers, load balancing, CI/CD, monitoring — not someone waiting on a platform team, because there isn't one - **A programming foundation beyond the main stack.** You can reach for Node or shell to build an automation workflow, an integration script or a sample app when the job needs one - **An instinct for scalability, reliability and fault tolerance.** Our customers are lenders and NBFCs — when something degrades, it degrades on someone's loan application **Nice to have** - Prior Go experience — it's a language you'll pick up in a few weeks either way - Orchestrating third-party APIs — retries, fallbacks, rate limits, and keeping things working when an upstream provider doesn't - Hands-on work with LLMs or agentic frameworks. If you've run an AI agent, a RAG setup or an MCP-based system in production rather than in a demo, say so — prototypes are everywhere right now, and having kept one alive under real traffic counts for a lot more. If you haven't, being strong on Python, AWS and API orchestration will get you there quickly enough **What we're looking for** - **1–2 years** building and shipping production software - **You like shipping.** The tenth version of something needs to work and be maintainable. It does not need to be beautiful - **Comfortable extending, ambitious about starting.** Early on you'll read what exists, understand the shape, and extend it — an instinct to rebuild everything first will get in the way. But we're not looking for someone who only follows a template either, because within six months you'll be starting things yourself - **Product sense.** Everything you build encodes something a real customer is trying to do. Understanding that is how you get it right the first time - **You ask good questions once, then focus.** Small team, limited review capacity - **Use AI tools freely** — own the decisions yourself. We expect you to ship faster with them, and we use them too. What we won't accept is code you can't explain, or an architecture you didn't choose. If you can't say why something works the way it does, it isn't finished **Being straight with you** Small team, Bangalore-based with two days a week in the office, no dedicated QA or DevOps. You'd be working directly alongside the engineer who built most of what exists, and with a founder. Early on, a lot of this work is building the next version of something that already exists. We think that's interesting — it's how a prototype becomes a product people pay for — and it's the fastest way to learn our systems. But it does mean the first few months aren't greenfield, and you should be fine with that. **Compensation** **₹12–15 lakh**, depending on what you've built before and how you do through the process — not years on a CV. **Process** 1. A call with the founder — the business, the role, your questions 2. A take-home assignment — roughly 4–8 hours of focused work. A small API, a simple hosted form, a data write. We want working software, not a design document 3. A session with our engineer — we walk through your assignment, then show you something real we've built and ask how you'd extend it 4. Final decision — a conversation on the offer, and we answer whatever's still open for you We move fast and we'll tell you where you stand at every stage. **Apply** Tell us something you've built and shipped, here(https://forms.gle/gAntgLBkDPifLydA9)

description: ## This is not a normal software engineering role At ClearFeed, using AI to build software is not optional. Every engineer is expected to use AI every day — to understand code, write code, review code, debug issues, design product flows, generate tests, write docs, explore APIs, and ship faster. We expect you to be comfortable using tools like Claude, Cursor, ChatGPT, Codex, or similar AI tools as part of your default engineering workflow. If you do not know how to use AI effectively to write code, debug issues, understand unfamiliar systems, and improve your own engineering output, **please do not apply**. We are looking for engineers who can use AI as leverage — while still bringing strong judgment, ownership, and engineering taste. AI can write a lot of the first draft. You are responsible for the final result. ## What we are building ClearFeed is building an AI-first support platform for modern teams working in Slack and Microsoft Teams. Our product connects conversations, tickets, knowledge bases, engineering tools, CRMs, and AI agents so companies can resolve customer and internal requests faster. Our engineers work on real product problems: * How should an AI agent understand a support conversation? * When should it answer automatically, and when should it ask a human? * How do we safely connect Slack, Teams, Zendesk, Jira, GitHub, Linear, Salesforce, HubSpot, and other tools? * How do we make AI workflows observable, debuggable, and trustworthy? * How do we ship fast without creating chaos for customers? ## What you will do You will take ambiguous customer problems and turn them into working software. That may include API design, backend logic, database changes, Slack/Teams workflows, AI-agent behavior, product UX, tests, monitoring, and deployment. You will be expected to: * Use AI tools heavily while writing and reviewing code. * Use AI to create first-pass designs, specs, implementation plans, tests, and docs. * Build backend services using TypeScript, Node.js, NestJS, PostgreSQL, Redis, queues, and cloud infrastructure. * Work on AI-agent features involving LLMs, RAG, tool-calling, structured outputs, evals, guardrails, and observability. * Own features end to end: idea → design → implementation → testing → release → production debugging. * Debug production issues and improve the system after every incident. * Improve our engineering system itself: better prompts, better internal tools, better test generation, better review loops, better deployment workflows. * Move fast, but stay accountable for what ships. ## What “AI-native” means here We do not mean “vibe code and hope it works.” We mean: * You can use AI to move significantly faster. * You can use AI to write, refactor, test, and debug code. * You can review AI-generated code critically. * You understand that AI is often confidently wrong. * You can use AI for product thinking, but you do not outsource judgment. * You can ship faster without lowering quality. * You can explain your decisions clearly to humans. The best engineers in the next decade will not be the ones who manually type the most code. They will be the ones who combine product judgment, technical depth, and AI leverage to ship high-quality software faster than traditional teams. ## What we are looking for You may be a good fit if: * You are already using AI coding tools daily. * You are faster today than you were one year ago because of AI. * You have strong software fundamentals and do not blindly trust generated code. * You can work across backend, product, integrations, and basic frontend when needed. * You care about customer experience, not just clean abstractions. * You enjoy working in small teams with high ownership. * You can take a problem statement and come back with a working solution. * You are comfortable with ambiguity. * You like shipping. * You are curious, direct, and low-ego. ## Bonus points We will pay extra attention if you have: * Built something real using AI agents. * Used Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, v0, Lovable, Replit, or similar tools seriously. * Shipped a side project using AI. * Built integrations with Slack, Teams, Zendesk, Jira, GitHub, Salesforce, or HubSpot. * Worked on support, developer tools, workflow automation, or B2B SaaS products. * Written about your engineering work. * Open-source contributions or visible proof of work. ## How we evaluate We use AI in our hiring process for the same reason we use it in engineering: it helps everyone move faster and spend time where human judgment matters most. The first step is a short AI-led interview of around 15 minutes. It helps us understand your background, your experience, and how you think about building software. After that, you will have three technical discussions with our team: * Problem solving + debugging * Problem solving * System design We want to understand how you reason, how you debug, how you make trade-offs, and how well you can combine engineering fundamentals with AI tools to build reliable software faster. ## What you get We want engineers to have the tools, support, and environment to do their best work. ### Flexible AI Credits You will get flexible AI credits and access to the tools you need to build faster — Claude, Cursor, ChatGPT, Codex, or whatever genuinely helps you ship better software. We do not want engineers hesitating before using AI because of subscription limits or tool access. ### Health and medical support You get comprehensive medical insurance, along with **free doctor consultations**. We are a small team, but we want to be thoughtful about health, family, and emergencies. You should not have to figure everything out on your own when something medical comes up. ### Sports and team activities We sponsor badminton and cricket games for the team. Not mandatory forced-fun activities. Just real sports, real games, and a good way to spend time with people outside tickets, PRs, and production issues. ## How to apply Apply here or send your resume to jobs@clearfeed.ai with: * Your LinkedIn, GitHub, or resume. * One thing you have built that you are proud of. * A short note on how you use AI in your engineering workflow. * Optional: a Loom/video/walkthrough of something you built.

Autofill Coverage owns the measurement of autofill quality end-to-end: establishing a manual baseline across top sites in every major category, automating that baseline into a repeatable regression and benchmarking suite, and reporting coverage, regressions, and competitive standing on a fixed cadence. As a Senior SDET on the Benchmarking side of the Autofill Coverage team, you'll own the automated performance monitoring and benchmarking harness for autofill, localizing regressions to specific merge commits, detecting them on main, and measuring worst-case performance under stress. Autofill already monitors correctness via BIT; you'll build out the three categories that extend it: - **Experience Impact:** What autofill costs the page, regardless of whether it fills anything - **Responsiveness:** How quickly autofill reacts to what a user does - **Predictability:** How stable autofill's behavior is as a whole, run to run and page to page, rather than any single cost or latency figure When your regression suite finds a mapping defect, you hand it to the Dataset engineers on this team to fix in Map the Web; when it finds anything else, you own routing it to the right team. You'll also work closely with the US Autofill team on triage, instrumentation standards, and release coordination. **WHAT YOU WILL DO** - Design and maintain benchmark scenarios that exercise autofill against busy, mutating, animation-heavy, and deeply-nested pages, using the browser's own performance-timeline tooling rather than active telemetry. - Build and maintain the underlying test instrumentation, including in-page signals for long-running or delayed rendering work, and custom timing marks the extension emits itself. Some of this data can only be captured in our own controlled test environment, using a debugging connection to the browser that isn't available on a real user's machine. You'll need to understand which signals are which, and design the harness accordingly. - Own the statistical model behind regression detection. - Correctly interpret and represent raw engine counters (e.g., heap size, node counts, GC pause) as what they actually are: paired before/after readings, not silently-derived deltas, and know when a signal is meaningful to gate on versus merely reportable. - Design join keys and event-record schemas so that independent signals (e.g., dropped frames and GC pauses) captured by different subsystems and clocks can be correlated and ordered against each other. - Build and maintain the harness's read side: consuming a scenario's own declared lifecycle and event marks from the performance timeline, rather than inferring state from rendered DOM output, so runs are comparable and captures remain valid to re-check later. - Publish results to Datadog, build alerting on benchmark regressions, and help localize a detected regression to the specific merge commit that introduced it. - Maintain the test-the-web scenario library and its marking conventions, and write Claude skills/documentation so the monitoring strategy stays correctly applied as new autofill code is added. - **Technical Stack:** Strong TypeScript; familiarity with browser extension architecture is a plus, since these benchmarks instrument the autofill content-script codebase directly. - **Observability Tooling:** Experience publishing metrics to and alerting from a platform like Datadog. - **Open Source & Communication:** Excellent written communication and a strong passion for open-source software, developer tooling, and modern internet security. ### **Why Join Us** This is an opportunity to play a foundational role in shaping our India Engineering COE from the ground up. description: Bitwarden promotes better internet security and safety with the leading open source password management solution for individuals, teams, and business organizations. Our philosophy on security is that “we are all in this together” – we continue to offer a full-featured free version of Bitwarden so that everyone can be protected with strong password management. We also provide enterprise-grade solutions to some of the largest companies in the world, and will continue to innovate in the identity and authentication market as the world starts to grow beyond passwords. Read more on [the Bitwarden blog](https://bitwarden.com/blog/). Autofill Coverage owns the measurement of autofill quality end-to-end: establishing a manual baseline across top sites in every major category, automating that baseline into a repeatable regression and benchmarking suite, and reporting coverage, regressions, and competitive standing on a fixed cadence. As a Senior Software Engineer on the Dataset side of this team, you'll own Map the Web, the curated dataset that establishes ground truth for how real-world login and signup forms are structured. Map the Web is the foundation that Fill Assist is built on, Bitwarden's targeted, rules-based system that resolves autofill issues on specific sites by layering vetted, site-specific field mappings on top of our standard heuristic qualification engine, even for forms that are out of alignment with the official spec. When regression testing (run by your SDET counterparts) surfaces a mapping defect, you own the fix in the dataset; when it surfaces anything else, you own routing it to the right team. **WHAT YOU WILL DO** - Own the ongoing curation, accuracy, and coverage of the Map the Web dataset across top sites in every major login/signup category, including the underlying targeted rules that power Fill Assist. - Design and maintain the data model and versioning strategy for site-specific field mappings, including backward-compatibility guarantees across supported browser client versions. - Build and maintain tooling and process for validating rule quality and safety before publication since faulty rules currently bypass heuristic fallback entirely. - Triage inbound reports of autofill defects (support tickets, regression findings) to determine whether a fix belongs in Map the Web or should be handed off to another team, and own the attributed hand-off when it's the latter. - Partner with the Autofill Coverage SDETs to close the loop between automated regression/benchmarking results and dataset updates. - Maintain the Map the Web repository (github.com/bitwarden/map-the-web) as a well-documented, contributor-friendly project, including guidance for how the dataset's rules interact with client-side fetching, sync, and storage. - Monitor how the dataset scales over time and flag technical debt or maintenance-burden risks early as this is a known failure mode from prior public-rules efforts (e.g. BIT tests, Equivalent Domains) that this team is explicitly designed to avoid repeating. - Work closely with the US Autofill team on validation standards. **WHAT YOU BRING** - **Overall Experience:** 6-10 years in Software Engineering. - **Web Forms & DOM Expertise:** Strong practical knowledge of HTML form structure, CSS selectors, and the ways real-world login/signup pages diverge from spec (nonstandard field identifiers, dynamically rendered forms, hidden/irrelevant fields). - **Dataset/Data Pipeline Experience:** Experience building and maintaining a structured, versioned dataset at scale to keep a large, evolving corpus accurate over time. - **Technical Stack:** Proficiency in TypeScript; familiarity with browser extension architecture (state/storage services, sync mechanisms) is a plus given this dataset feeds directly into browser client behavior. - **Quality & Validation Mindset:** Experience designing automated or semi-automated grading/validation systems to catch bad data before it ships, rather than relying on manual review alone. - **Security Awareness:** Basic understanding of the security posture differences between vetted, human-authored rules and heuristic-based autofill. - **Open Source & Communication:** Excellent written communication and a strong passion for open-source software, developer tooling, and modern internet security. ### **Why Join Us** This is an opportunity to play a foundational role in shaping our India Engineering COE from the ground up. Our user community loves us and we love them. Come to work each day with a sense of purpose as we bring a more secure internet experience to everyone from our friends and family to the world’s largest organizations. Become an expert. You’ll get immersed in the prominent technology markets of security and open source software. You'll work alongside talented global teams, solve meaningful engineering challenges, influence how we scale our engineering organization & contribute to products used by customers around the world. If you're passionate about building exceptional teams, enabling engineering excellence, and making a lasting impact within a fast-growing engineering company, we'd love to hear from you. ### **Equal Opportunity Employer** We are committed to fostering an inclusive workplace where everyone can do their best work. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and make employment decisions based on skills, experience, qualifications, and business needs.

description: **Role Overview** We are looking for a Software Engineer who is genuinely strong at mathematics and enjoys turning that mathematics into working software. You will develop algorithms for gimbal and sensor calibration applications. The role covers the full path from mathematical model to deployed code, modelling, algorithm development, simulation, analysis, and a robust C/C++ implementation that holds up against real measurements. If you like problems where the answer has to be both mathematically correct and numerically well-behaved, this will suit you. **Key Responsibilities** • Design and implement mathematically intensive algorithms, with an emphasis on numerical accuracy and robustness. • Develop algorithms involving 2D and 3D geometry, coordinate transformations, rotation matrices and other rotation representations, camera parameters and sensor orientation. • Convert measurements between image, sensor, platform and world coordinate systems. • Process data from cameras, gimbals and multiple sensors, including data that is noisy, incomplete or asynchronous. • Handle timing and synchronization across subsystems - sensor latency, processing delays, clock differences and missing data. • Implement recursive estimation techniques that maintain a running best estimate of system state as successive noisy measurements arrive, including prediction between updates and handling of the associated uncertainty. • Apply filtering, smoothing and numerical methods - interpolation, integration, iterative solvers, least-squares fitting to produce stable results from imperfect input. • Analyze recorded datasets, evaluate algorithm accuracy against reference data, and quantify sources of error. • Build Python and Qt-based tooling for simulation, visualization and analysis to support algorithm development and validation. • Optimize algorithms for accuracy, robustness and real-time performance. • Work closely with the computer vision, imaging, embedded and systems teams. **Required Skills** **Mathematics** A strong working command of most of the following, and the ability to derive results rather than only apply library functions: • Linear algebra; vector and matrix mathematics • Trigonometry, 2D and 3D geometry • Coordinate transformations and rotation representations • Numerical methods and optimization • Error analysis and uncertainty estimation • Signal processing fundamentals Above all, you should be able to take a mathematical model and turn it into software that behaves correctly outside of ideal conditions. **Software Engineering** • Strong C/C++ programming skills, particularly in numerical or algorithm-heavy code. • Good working knowledge of Python for prototyping, simulation and data analysis. • Experience with Qt for building desktop tools, visualization utilities and operator-facing interfaces. • Comfortable working in a Linux development environment, with CMake, Git and standard build and debugging tooling. • Ability to write clean, maintainable and testable code. **Qualifications** A Bachelor's or Master's in Computer Science, Mathematics, Applied Mathematics, Robotics, Mechanical Engineering, Control Systems or a related field.
